# 18 Give the sequence diagram its default theme

## Outcome

A sequence diagram rendered in a real browser is actually visible and legible: lifelines,
message arrows, block frames, participant boxes, actor icons, destroy marks, box-group
backgrounds, the title and autonumber labels all pick up colors, strokes and type from
`packages/core/src/theme/default.css`'s existing `--siren-*` design tokens, the same way the
flowchart's `.siren-node`/`.siren-edge` rules already do.

## Why this ticket exists

Found in the board's closing review. `theme/default.css` carries rules only for `.siren-node`,
`.siren-edge`, the arrow marker fill and the animation classes — nothing for any of the nine
sequence-diagram classes the renderer emits. SVG defaults then apply: `<line>`/`<path>` elements
have no stroke and are invisible, and `<rect>` elements fill black, so a participant box renders
as a black slab with black label text on it. Every one of the board's 170 tests still passes,
because jsdom never paints — this criterion is structurally invisible to the test suite, which is
why it survived seventeen tickets. spec.md's acceptance criterion "`demos/sequence-diagram.html`
... visibly renders a sequence diagram exercising every feature in scope" does not currently hold.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every class the sequence renderer emits has a theme rule: `.siren-participant` (its `rect`
  and `text`), the actor stick-figure shapes, `.siren-lifeline`, `.siren-message-arrow`,
  `.siren-message-label`, `.siren-autonumber`, `.siren-block-frame`, `.siren-block-divider`,
  `.siren-block-label`, `.siren-block-fill`, `.siren-box` background and label,
  `.siren-destroy-mark`, `.siren-title`, and the `.siren-arrow-stroke` marker paths used by the
  cross and open arrowheads.
- [ ] Rules are expressed through the existing `--siren-*` custom properties, adding new tokens
  only where a genuinely new concept needs one (e.g. a lifeline's dash color). No hardcoded
  colors outside the token declarations, per ADR-0004.
- [ ] The lifeline renders dashed, and message arrows keep the `stroke-dasharray` the renderer
  sets for `dotted` line styles — the theme must not override the per-message dash the renderer
  applies inline.
- [ ] A `rect` block's inline `fill` (the author's own `rgb(...)` color) still wins over the
  theme, and an uncolored `.siren-box` background falls back to a theme color.
- [ ] Both light and the existing dark-theme token set are covered — the demos' theme toggle
  produces a legible diagram in both.
- [ ] `demos/sequence-diagram.html` opened in a browser shows all three examples legibly.

## Test seam

CSS is not unit-testable in jsdom (it never paints), and this board has no browser-automation
dependency — the same gap that let the defect through. So: assert what *is* checkable, and
verify the rest visually.

- Checkable: a test asserting every class name the renderer emits has at least one matching
  selector in `theme/default.css`, so a future renderer class cannot silently ship unthemed.
  Read the stylesheet as a string via Vite's `?raw` import (the package has no `@types/node`).
- Visual: rasterize the rendered SVG with the stylesheet inlined and look at it. Report what you
  saw. Do not claim a visual check you did not perform.

## Write ownership

- `packages/core/src/theme/default.css`
- `packages/core/src/theme/*.test.ts` (new, for the class-coverage test)
- `packages/core/src/renderer/renderSequenceToSVG.ts` (only if a class hook is genuinely
  missing — say so explicitly rather than restructuring the renderer)
